html:
The Bega, better known as the Beja, are a Cushitic-speaking people of the Red Sea hills, between the Nile and the coast, in what is now eastern Sudan, southeastern Egypt and Eritrea. They are shown here in 700.

They were herders of camels, cattle and goats in a dry, rugged land, and many scholars link them to older desert peoples such as the Medjay and the Blemmyes. The hills held gold and emerald mines, which drew Egyptian, Roman and later Arab prospectors. In 700 they lived between Christian Nubia, Aksum and the new Muslim rulers of Egypt, raiding and trading with all of them. Over the following centuries they slowly took up Islam, and ports such as Suakin grew on their coast.
